e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian form of Naomi, from Hebrew no'omi, my pleasantness. In the Bible Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth.
A modern American coinage that adds the -ly ending of Kimberly and Everly to Ember, the word for a glowing coal.
A diminutive of the Roman name Prisca, from Latin priscus, ancient. In the New Testament Priscilla is an early Christian leader and a friend of Paul.
namesakes: Priscilla Presley (actress and former wife of Elvis)

assoc.t: Priscilla Presley, actress and former wife of Elvis
Priscilla, 2023 Sofia Coppola film on Priscilla Presley
The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert

e.note: The nickname Prissy doubles as a word for fussy or prim.

e.etymology: A modern short form of Tatiana and Christiana, also used as a longer form of Tia. Disney chose it for the heroine of The Princess and the Frog (2009).

assoc.t: Disney princess in The Princess and the Frog

e.etymology: From mavis, an old poetic word for the song thrush, borrowed from Old French. Marie Corelli used it for a character in her 1895 novel The Sorrows of Satan, which launched it as a given name.

assoc.t: Mavis Beacon Teaches Typing software
Mavis, Dracula's daughter in Hotel Transylvania
Mavis Discount Tire shops

e.etymology: From Germanic Adalbert: adal, noble, and beraht, bright. It surged in the English-speaking world after Queen Victoria married Prince Albert in 1840.

assoc.t: Fat Albert, the 1970s cartoon character
Albert Einstein, physicist

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese form of Ralph and French Raoul, from a Germanic name built from words for counsel and wolf.
A phonetic spelling of the sound EYE-la, used as a respelling of Isla, the name taken from the Scottish island of Islay, and of the older Ila.
A modern American name in the style of Aaliyah and Mariyah, an elaboration of Zaria or Zara with the -iyah ending.
A short form of Alexandra and feminine of Alex, from Greek alexein, to defend, and aner, man. Its American use dropped sharply after Amazon named its voice assistant Alexa in 2014.

assoc.t: Amazon's voice assistant

e.note: Shares its name with Amazon's voice assistant, so it invites jokes and can wake smart speakers when called aloud.

e.etymology: Coined by George Lucas for Anakin Skywalker, the Jedi who becomes Darth Vader in Star Wars. American parents began using it in the 1990s.

assoc.t: Anakin Skywalker, who becomes Darth Vader in Star Wars

e.note: Everyone will connect it to Star Wars, where Anakin grows up to be the villain Darth Vader.

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Jason, influenced by Jay. Jason comes from Greek Iason, the hero who led the Argonauts, a name tied to the Greek verb for to heal.
From the English and Welsh surname meaning son of Davy, a medieval pet form of David, the Hebrew name meaning beloved.

assoc.t: Davis, California, home of UC Davis
Davis Cup, international men's tennis competition

e.etymology: A pet form of Abigail, Hebrew for my father is joy, also given as a full name. In the Bible Abigail is a wise woman who becomes a wife of King David.

assoc.t: Dear Abby, the long-running advice column
Abby, co-lead of The Last of Us Part II

e.etymology: A respelling of Journey, the English word, which comes from Old French journee, a day's travel or a day's work.

assoc.t: Journey, the rock band behind Don't Stop Believin'

e.etymology: From an English surname that goes back to the Old English name Ealdwine: eald, old, and wine, friend. John Alden came to Plymouth on the Mayflower.
namesakes: Alden Ehrenreich (actor, Solo: A Star Wars Story)

e.etymology: Popularized by Jovie, the department-store elf played by Zooey Deschanel in the 2003 film Elf. It is linked to jovial, from Latin jovialis, of Jupiter.

assoc.t: Jovie, Buddy's love interest in the movie Elf
Bon Jovi, the rock band and singer (same sound)

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins the fashionable Brae- or Bray- sound to the -lynn ending, alongside Braylen and Braylon.
A 19th-century short form of Adela and Adelaide, Germanic names built on adal, noble. It also served as a pet form of Delia.
namesakes: Della Reese (singer and Touched by an Angel star)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian form of Gerard, from the Germanic words ger, spear, and hard, brave or hardy.

assoc.t: Gerardo, singer of the 1990 hit Rico Suave

e.etymology: From Greek Kassandra, the Trojan princess of myth who foretold the future but was cursed never to be believed. The root meaning of the name is uncertain.
namesakes: Cassandra Peterson (Elvira, Mistress of the Dark)
Cassandra Clare (author of The Mortal Instruments)

assoc.t: Trojan prophetess of Greek myth whom no one believed
a Cassandra, someone whose true warnings are ignored
Apache Cassandra database software

e.meaning: Arabic form of Moses, traditionally drawn out of the water
e.etymology: The Arabic form of Moses, the prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt, honored in Islam, Judaism and Christianity. Exodus ties the name to a Hebrew verb for drawing out of water.

e.meaning: one sent ahead to explore and report
e.etymology: The English word scout, from Old French escouter, to listen. As a name it comes from Scout Finch, the young narrator of Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird (1960).
namesakes: Scout Willis (daughter of Bruce Willis and Demi Moore)

assoc.t: Scout Finch, narrator of To Kill a Mockingbird
Boy Scouts and Girl Scouts
Scout, the revived off-road truck brand

e.note: Scout is also a popular name for dogs.

e.etymology: A feminine form of David, the Hebrew name meaning beloved, made with the ending -ina. It arose in Scotland.
From the Roman family name Marinus, long tied to Latin marinus, of the sea. Saint Marina was an early martyr venerated in the Orthodox Church.
namesakes: Marina Sirtis (Star Trek: The Next Generation actress)

assoc.t: marina, a harbor for small boats and yachts
Marina del Rey; San Francisco's Marina District

e.etymology: The Latin word for glory. It was long a Spanish and Portuguese devotional name, as Maria de Gloria, and entered English use through 19th-century fiction.

assoc.t: Gloria, the 1982 Laura Branigan hit song
Gloria in excelsis Deo, the Christian hymn
Gloria Pritchett on Modern Family

e.meaning: form of Arthur, often linked to a Celtic word for bear
e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian form of Arthur, the name of the legendary British king. Its root is debated: a Celtic word for bear or the Roman family name Artorius.
In the US mostly the Swahili word for purpose, the fifth principle of Kwanzaa. Nia is also a Welsh name, a form of Irish Niamh, bright, and a short form of Antonia.
namesakes: Nia Vardalos (writer and star of My Big Fat Greek Wedding)

assoc.t: Nia, purpose, the fifth principle of Kwanzaa

e.etymology: The Basque form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, manly, introduced by the Basque writer Sabino Arana. In the US it also reads as a clipping of Anderson or Alexander.
From an English surname and Cheshire place name: an Old English personal name plus leah, a woodland clearing. It is best known from Aldous Huxley, author of Brave New World.

assoc.t: Aldous Huxley, author of Brave New World (surname)

e.etymology: A modern coinage built on amour, the French word for love, with a feminine -a ending. It is a spelling of Amora.
An English form of Irish Eibhlin, itself from Norman French Aveline, which makes it a cousin of Evelyn. It has featured in classic Irish songs.

assoc.t: Come On Eileen, 1982 hit by Dexys Midnight Runners
